title: AN/BYG-1 Applications
description: Description NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company�s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click �My Profile�, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand �E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)�, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click �Send.� For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). Classified material will be dispatched via USPS Registered Mail (or Government-approved commercial express carrier authorized for Secret transport). A double-envelope system will be utilized. The outer envelope will feature no classification markings. A signed Classified Material Receipt will be enclosed

description: Solicitation Notice: 36C79126R0011 � Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program Notice Type: Solicitation Issuance Notice Solicitation Number: 36C79126R0011 Posted Date: September 18, 2026 Response Due Date: October 19, 2026, 3:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) NAICS Code: 334510 � Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. This NAICS code is appropriate as it encompasses the manufacturing of FDA?regulated electromedical therapeutic equipment including TENS, IFC, neuromodulation, and diathermy devices. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). Tier-3 Other Small Business Concerns: If no award can be made at Tier-3, the Government will evaluate offers from all Other-Than-Small-Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses)) in Tier 4 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101?3 and 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Tier-4 Other?Than?Small Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses): If no award can be made under any small business Tier 1 through 3, the Government will evaluate offers from other?than?small businesses or large business concerns in Tier 4. This tiered evaluation methodology is authorized under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and implemented through the VA�s Class Deviation to VAAR 815.101?370, which permits the use of tiered set?aside procedures to minimize procurement delays in situations where market research indicates that award at the SDVOSB or VOSB tiers is uncertain. Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs, Enterprise Procurement Office, Acquisition Service Four Delta Team, 555 Corporate Circle, Golden, CO 80401-5621. Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is pleased to announce the release of Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011, the official Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. Key Dates: RFP Questions Due-In Date: On or before but no later than October 5, 2026, at 3:00 PM CDT, questions received after this deadline may receive a Government response or receipt acknowledgement. Proposal Package and Product Samples Due-In Date: On or before but no later than October 19, 2026, at 3:00 PM CDT. Early proposal package and product samples are encouraged. Anticipated Award: The results of competition ultimately determine when and if award(s) can be made, but the VA intends to finalize award decisions on or before but no later than January 19, 2027, the expiration date of the legacy TENS contract. The VA reserves the right not to make an award or to make award on some CLINs/SLINs but not all the CLINs/SLINs enumerated in the solicitation. Proposal Package Submission Instructions: A responsive proposal is one that conforms to the solicitation in all material respects and complies fully with all instructions contained therein, including but not limited to Offerors� certifications, representations, submission formatting, inclusion of all mandatory documentation, and the shipment of product samples to the VA�s Denver Logistic Services facility in Golden, Colorado in accordance with the product samples delivery requirements as stated throughout the RFP. Submission of a proposal package in response to Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011 is strictly voluntary. All costs associated with the preparation, development, and submission of proposals, proposal package documentation, and any required product samples shall be borne solely by the Offeror. The Department of Veterans Affairs will not reimburse, compensate, or otherwise pay Offerors for any expenses incurred in the preparation or submission of proposal materials or product samples. Offerors shall not invoice the Government for such costs. All proposal preparation and submission activities are performed at the Offeror�s own expense. Policy Note: In the event of a conflict between this Solicitation Notice posted at the Government-wide Point of Entry (GPE) website at https://www.sam.gov and solicitation number 36C79126R0011, the solicitation shall prevail, govern, and control. The affected parts are wholly owned by FMS customer countries, are not covered by a Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangement (CLSSA), these same assets will be delivered to the customer country for their sole use. The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. The FMS customer countries retain ownership of their parts throughout the asset's lifecycle. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. Based on this, there is no need for these non-CLSSA FMS country assets to be specially marked for tracking by DoD. \

Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. In the event that the failed assembly is found to be beyond economical repair (BER), as defined in the contract, or in the event that the Government equipment is received with one or more subassemblies missing (FOR EXAMPLE: AS ARESULT OF CANNABALIZATION BY AN AIRCRAFT OPERATING SITE),the contractor shall promptly obtain confirmation of such findings from the cognizant DCMC QAR. and upon confirmation promptly notify the PCO for authority to scrap if BER and,if missing subassemblies, proceed IAW Missing on Induction (MOI).Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing parts are received or unless specifically authorized by the PCO. All disassembly, repair and assembly of the Government equipment shall be IAW current engineering drawings and configuration specifications. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Replaced hardware shall be in accordance with the latest drawing revisions.The contractor shall provide and may use new or repaired/reworked parts which meet the requirements of the repair specification to restore the Government equipment in the delivery time specified in the contract. Repaired/reworked parts shall be used in lieu of new whenever possible as allowed by the applicable repair specification.Any repair of lower assemblies and/or detail parts not authorized by the by the applicable repair specification shall be submitted to the QAR for Government review and approval.Requests for repair approvals shall be accompanied by details of the repair and other applicable data such as tests which have been performed to validate the repair. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REQUIREMENTS GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall provide at the contractors facility the necessary repair labor, new and serviceable reworked repair parts, materials and test equipmentand arrange for outside services as required to return the equipment to a serviceable condition within the calendar day shop time as specified in the delivery schedule of the contract. SCOPE OF WORK FOR REPAIR: The scope of the work in the following subparagraphs are applicable to the latest configuration of the Government equipment.There shall be a 100% repair rate on all CLIN carcasses. Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. In the event that the failed assembly is found to be beyond economical repair (BER), as defined in the contract, or in the event that the Government equipment is received with one or more subassemblies missing (FOR EXAMPLE: AS ARESULT OF CANNABALIZATION BY AN AIRCRAFT OPERATING SITE),the contractor shall promptly obtain confirmation of such findings from the cognizant DCMC QAR. and upon confirmation promptly notify the PCO for authority to scrap if BER and,if missing subassemblies, proceed IAW Missing on Induction (MOI).Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing parts are received or unless specifically authorized by the PCO. All disassembly, repair and assembly of the Government equipment shall be IAW current engineering drawings and configuration specifications. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Replaced hardware shall be in accordance with the latest drawing revisions.The contractor shall provide and may use new or repaired/reworked parts which meet the requirements of the repair specification to restore the Government equipment in the delivery time specified in the contract. Repaired/reworked parts shall be used in lieu of new whenever possible as allowed by the applicable repair specification.Any repair of lower assemblies and/or detail parts not authorized by the by the applicable repair specification shall be submitted to the QAR for Government review and approval.Requests for repair approvals shall be accompanied by details of the repair and other applicable data such as tests which have been performed to validate the repair. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REPAIR PARTS: The contractor shall be responsible for identification, selection, ordering, and stocking of required piece parts to support all repairs. By definition," piece part" shall be any part or material listed in the applicable repair specification. TEST EQUIPMENT: The contractor will provide a laboratory facility equipped with instrumentation and testing capability for comprehensive functional testing of the equipment and detailed inspections of subassemblies and detailed parts. The contractor test equipment shall be designed to ensure repaired Government equipment function in full compliance with the requirementsof the applicable repair specification. All Government equipment's electrical performance and mechanical parameters shall be measured in accordance with the requirements of the applicable repair specification,with hard copy reports of all measurements available to the Government upon request. title: Bulgaria – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – „Развитие и въвеждане на Институционална архитектура на АМ по отношение на Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа (СУИД)“
description: Предметът и обемът на обществената поръчка включва изпълнението на следните дейности: 1. Основна дейност 1: „Развитие на Институционална архитектура на АМ по отношение на Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа (СУИД)“; 2. Основна дейност 2: „Въвеждане на Институционалната архитектура на Агенция „Митници“ по отношение на Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа (СУИД)“, чрез: Надградена 1 бр. Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа в съответствие със съюзните функционални изисквания, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8; Реализирана 1 бр. интеграция на СУИД със Системата за директен достъп на търговците до европейските ИС UUM&DS, Release 2.8; Актуализирани версии на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) до последните актуални версии, издадени от производителя и реинженеринг на СУИД при необходимост; Актуализирани, при необходимост 2 бр. спецификации, свързани със СУИД, във връзка с изискванията, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8, последните актуални версии на готовите решения на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) и надграждане на съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД; Надградени съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД; Запазени съществуващи интеграции на СУИД с митническите информационни системи, националните регистри (Търговски регистър, Регистър Булстат, Регистър Национална база данни „Население“ и Регистър Единен регистър на чужденците) и RegiX, и при необходимост надграждане на интеграциите с изискванията, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8, последните актуални версии на готовите решения на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) и надграждане на съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД. 3. Основна дейност 3: „Обучение на 50 служители на АМ (10 приложни администратори, 5 системни администратори, 5 потребители за регистрации на ИО в Е-Портала на АМ и 30 потребители с права на ръководител) за работа с реализираните функционалности по дейността“.

Η προμήθεια του πληροφοριακού συστήματος καλύπτει τις επιχειρησιακές λειτουργείες της Περιφέρειας που αφορούν στη Διαχείριση Ανθρώπινου Δυναμικού, στη Διαχείριση Οικονομικών Πόρων και στη Διαχείριση Επιχειρησιακού Σχεδίου και Έργων.

title: J030--Generator-ATS Maintenance (VA-27-00002745)
description: What are the hours of operation for Generator Maintenance? This is in the SOW Can you provide a Document with each Back-up Generator Model # s &Serial # s? This is Attachment A of the package Please Confirm the Voltage of the Generators? 480 and 240 Regarding Contractor Provided Consumables, many of the items listed are typically repairs quoted and approved before work proceeds on this and some parts(hoses and belts). As an outside vendor there is no way to effectively build this into your maintenance plan to guarantee effective cost for both the vendor and for Edward Hines VA. We request this section is altered to allow for these costs to be sectioned out for repairs and for one annual service to replace filters and oil.� See Attachment B. How many Generators have Diesel Engines?� All of them Are there any Generators with difficulty accessing (Roof, Parking Garage, Basement)? If so, which units are they? NO Are your Generators within 50 ft of the Entry Door, where our truck will be parked? Yes Are the Annual Load Tests performed with your Minor B-PMs? No Can I get the age of each equipment if possible? See Attachment A Please clarify the Unscheduled Repair CLIN amount. Is the stated $50,000 intended to mean $50,000 per contract year? This is just a funding item for me to populate an unscheduled maintenance clin for me to address items the break. Where should emergency travel and labor be priced? All previous contracts has local labor. Never had this issue. Build it in your quote. Will VA furnish diesel consumed during inspections? VA furnishes Fuel for the generators Period. Can you provide any previous maintenance reports, emergency calls, major repairs, etc.? After Award. Consumables Attachment Section 2.1 states Replace PM Consumables as required and references Attachment 1, while the solicitation package includes Generator Consumables Attachment B. Please confirm that Attachment B is the document intended by the reference to Attachment 1, and that the consumables identified in Attachment B are to be furnished and replaced by the contractor as required during preventive maintenance and included within the applicable PM CLIN pricing. Consumables are outlined in Attachment B. Work Hours / Load Bank Testing Section 4.3 identifies the monthly PM for the two 600 kW generators and one 500 kW generator as occurring on the second Tuesday of each month from 4:00 AM to 7:00 AM, while the 1250 kW and 750 kW generators may be serviced during normal business hours. Please confirm whether the annual load-bank testing, ATS maintenance, sampling, and other annual maintenance activities may also be performed during normal business hours unless otherwise coordinated with the COR. The 600 s, and 500 are backing up a critical production line that is old and has issues during power transfers. We require them and their associated equipment to be cycled or maintained prior to that department s workday start, so they can start the production line on time with no delay. This department is the Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacy (CMOP). All the generator maintenance is to be performed on the second Tuesday of each month, we need the CMOP Generators started and done first. Transformer Annual Inspection and IR Scan The scope includes quarterly energized transformer inspections as well as an annual inspection that includes additional maintenance activities and an IR scan. The pricing schedule only provides a quarterly transformer CLIN with a quantity of four. Please confirm whether the annual transformer inspection and IR scan are to be included within the pricing for the four quarterly inspections, with one quarterly service incorporating the annual work, or if the annual service is to be priced separately. Please confirm the intended operating condition for the annual IR scan, as it appears under the annual de-energized inspection section. Annual Transformer and ATS IR Scanning Procedure The annual infrared (IR) scan of transformer lugs and automatic transfer switches (ATSs) is to be completed while the equipment is energized, prior to any deenergizing procedures. This approach allows for the identification of potential faults under operating conditions, ensuring that any issues are detected before maintenance begins. Once the IR scan is performed, any necessary repairs should be made during the scheduled deenergized maintenance period. This ensures that faults identified during the scan can be addressed safely while the equipment is not under load. The IR scan should occur once each year and, whenever possible, should be scheduled close to the time of the annual deenergized maintenance. This coordination facilitates efficient fault resolution and minimizes downtime. In the event of an emergent issue identified during the scan, immediate corrective action will be taken to address the problem as soon as possible, regardless of the scheduled maintenance cycle.

title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production
description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO�s and TDPs.

description: The Defense Logistics Agency-Aberdeen, on behalf of the Army Integrated Logistics Supply Center (ILSC) � Supply Chain Management Directorate (SCMD) � Strategic Sourcing Directorate (SSD), intends to acquire Parts to support the Load, Bank, Electrical. Requirements Description: The load bank is a piece of electrical test equipment used to simulate an electrical load, to test an electric power source. The load bank is used to provide field preventive maintenance checks and services of the Electric Power Plant (EPP III) on the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The EPP III is the main electric power source for the PATRIOT Missile Defense System. The load banks are used on the 15 KW,30KW, and 150 KW, 400Hz generator sets on the EPP III. The load banks must meet the requirements of the CECOM Purchase Description (PD) #A3357168 Rev A and A3354293 Rev A. The PD can be obtained by writing via email to david.teicher.civ@army.mil.We are looking for brand name or equal load banks meeting the requirements of the PD, at a minimum, which will also include load cables. Detailed technical data for the manufacture or acceptance of this item is not available from the Army. The Government does not possess the technical data package (TDP) for the parts. title: Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

description: Auf dem Gelände der Marineunteroffizierschule in Plön ist der Bau von zwei neuen Unterkunftsgebäuden geplant, Gebäude 47 und Gebäude 54. Diese werden auf zwei separaten, nicht miteinander verbundenen Baufeldern auf der Liegenschaft erstellt. Die Erschließung erfolgt über das Haupttor der Kaserne. Die Flächen sind verkehrstechnisch über die befestigten Straßenflächen innerhalb des Geländes erschlossen. Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 47 soll auf einer ehemaligen Waldfläche an der südöstlichen Grenze des Geländes realisiert werden. Das Grundstück wird im Rahmen des Bauvorhabens an die bestehende Infrastruktur der Liegenschaft angeschlossen. Das Baufeld umfasst ca. 5.860m². Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 54 ist auf der Fläche zwischen den Gebäuden 53 und der RÜH (Rettungsübungshalle) geplant. Das Grundstück ist an die bestehende Infrastruktur der Liegenschaft angeschlossen. Das Baufeld umfasst ca. 2.400m². Die viergeschossigen Gebäude mit einer Gesamtabmessung von 57,70 m x 14,16 m sind mit einem 43° geneigten Satteldach versehen und werden über zwei Treppenräume an der Längsseite erschlossen. Die Traufhöhe beträgt 10,50 m, die Firsthöhe beträgt 17,10 m. Es handelt sich um Massivbauten mit Mauerwerkswänden, Stahlbetondecken und einem Dachstuhl in Holzbauweise. In jedem Neubau sind jeweils 81 Einzelunterkünfte untergebracht. Für die Dauer des BVH im Zeitraum ca. III. Q 2026 bis ca. IV. Q 2028 ist eine übergeordnete Baustelleneinrichtung sowie deren Vorhaltung auf dem Baufeld 47 geplant und in einem separaten Leistungsverzeichnis erfasst. Ein Fassadengerüst wird für die Dauer der Maßnahme zur Verfügung gestellt und ist in einem separaten Leistungsverzeichnis erfasst. Es gelten die Sicherheitsauflagen für militärische Anlagen.
